newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu insists he will make peace with Syria.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu insists he will make peace with Syria.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu vowed on Wednesday he would make the peace with Syria that evaded his Israeli predecessors, despite his refusal to give up the occupied Golan Heights.

"I am certain that in our way we will succeed at the task that our predecessors did not succeed at and bring about peace with Syria," the Israeli leader told a parliamentary debate to mark 30 years of Jewish settlement on the Golan.

Only this week Israel's air force intelligence chief said the probability of war with the Arabs could no longer be characterised as low and that Syria remained "Israel's number one confrontation state".

Syria, demanding the return of the heights, has assailed Netanyahu for rejecting the land-for-peace policy of the left-leaning government he ousted in May and for backing Jewish settlement on the plateau occupied since a 1967 war.
Addressing settlers as his friends, Netanyahu said: "May you be blessed and strengthened". He said the Golan was as essential to Israel's water supply as for its security.

He repeated his prediction of a peace deal with Syria by the end of his first term in the year 2000 but demanded that Syria stop guerrilla attacks against Israel from Lebanon, where Damascus is the main power broker with 30,000 troops.

"We view the Golan as an area essential to the security of the state of Israel, by the way not just the physical military security but rather also as a territory with decisive importance for the water system of the state of Israel," he said.

Israel will soon begin selling land on the occupied Golan Heights in order to expand the Jewish settlement of Katzrin by 96 homes, an Israeli spokesman said on Monday. Israel's leading Peace Now movement blasted the decision as a "countdown to war".

Five years of sporadic peace talks between Israel and Syria over the fate of the plateau have yet to resume under Netanyahu, and Israelis have grown jittery as a war of words between the arch-foes has heated up.
Israel's previous Labour party leaders the late Yitzhak Rabin and Shimon Peres were prepared to make at least a partial pullback from the Golan in exchange for peace.
